newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA'S BIG HITTERS PILE UP 339-4.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA'S BIG HITTERS PILE UP 339-4.

text.p: Sanath Jayasuriya and Aravinda De Silva led a batting onslaught as world champions Sri Lanka piled up 339 for four in the first final of the Independence Cup tournament against Pakistan on Saturday.
Opener Jayasuriya smashed 96 from 67 balls and De Silva 90 at exactly a run a ball.
Skipper Arjuna Ranatunga, who won the toss, then lent support with an elegant 80.
Jayasuriya, who completed 3,000 runs in 123 innings in 131 one-day internationals, hit 12 boundaries and a six and punished Pakistan for twice putting down catches.

He had made only five when Saeed Anwar at cover put down a difficult chance off the bowling of paceman Aaqib Javed. Later Abdul Razzak dropped a simple catch at backward point off leg-spinner Shahid Afridi's bowling point when Jayasuriya was on 58.

Jayasuriya and Marvan Atapattu put on 148, a record opening partnership for Sri Lanka against any opposition, before Jayasuriya was finally caught by substitute Mohammed Wasim at deep mid-off, attempting a second six in one over off left-arm spinner Mohammed Hussain.
Soon afterwards, Hussain trapped Atapattu leg before after he had made 53 off 72 balls.
De Silva, who hit 10 fours and a six, added 153 off 130 balls for the third wicket with Ranatunga who 70-ball innings included a delightful array of wristy strokes and glances.
De Silva and Ranatunga were both stumped by Moin Khan off Saqlain Mushtaq almost at the end of their 50 overs.
